# Polo: how Coachella actually works

> A cited, independent deep dive on how the Coachella festival works - the grounds (Empire Polo Club), polo itself, the stages, the 2006 Daft Punk pyramid, the moments, the transport system, camping rituals, the lineup, the build, the money, the desert season and an archive of artist billboards on the I-10.

About 47,330 words, 610 sources, updated November 2026. Not affiliated with Coachella, Goldenvoice or AEG.

## Chapters
- [Prologue: a polo field and a boycott](https://polo.cold.fyi/prologue/): In November 1993, Pearl Jam would not play Los Angeles on Ticketmaster's terms, so a small punk promoter called Goldenvoice put them on a polo field in Indio for about 25,000 people. The field belonged to a shopping-center heir who loved polo. The valley it sits in is named after a printer's typo. Six years later, the promoter came back with a festival.
- [The beginning](https://polo.cold.fyi/beginning/): Goldenvoice was a punk promoter paid for by its founder's marijuana smuggling, handed to two young employees when he went to prison. Their first festival, in October 1999, drew about half the crowd they needed and lost $850K to $1M. Paul Tollett sold his house. Then they skipped a year, came back for one day, sold the company to AEG, and kept adding days until two identical weekends grossed $114.6M in 2017.
- [Every year](https://polo.cold.fyi/years/): Every edition on one page, from Pearl Jam's polo-field show in 1993 to the 2026 sellout. A $50 day ticket became a $649 weekend, two days became six, and the gross climbed to $114.6M in 2017 before the published numbers stopped. Three years are missing entirely, and most recent years have no official attendance at all.
- [The grounds](https://polo.cold.fyi/grounds/): For 22 years Coachella was a tenant, renting a polo club in Indio for a few weeks each spring and handing it back. Goldenvoice bought the land next door in 2012, and in 2021 took over the whole club year-round on a lease that runs to 2050. Somewhere between 78 and 1,000 acres, depending on who is counting, now flips from Coachella to Stagecoach in under a week.
- [The polo club](https://polo.cold.fyi/polo/): You pay a lot of money every year to hang out at a polo club, and the polo club stopped playing polo. It ended in November 2021, when Goldenvoice took over Empire year-round and staff got three days' notice. Desert polo lives on next door at Eldorado, on land Goldenvoice owns and leases back until the festival needs it. Here is how the game works, what the club was, and what the grounds do now when nobody is riding on them.
- [The stages and the spaces within](https://polo.cold.fyi/stages/): Coachella opened in 1999 with a main stage, a second stage and three tents named for deserts, and it has been adding rooms ever since. The Sahara has moved three times and now stands on 1,500 tons of concrete. Do LaB started as a broken water feature and grew into a stage with its own secret lineup and its own festival. Then come the nightclub tent, the punk tent, the sound system with seven stacks, a dome, a beer house and a brand-new stage built in under four months.
- [Daft Punk and the pyramid](https://polo.cold.fyi/pyramid/): In 2006 Daft Punk said yes to Coachella after a year of saying no, because their manager, who usually turned offers down without asking them, picked up the phone. They played the Sahara tent at 11 p.m. on a Saturday, inside a pyramid of LED blocks built for that one show. The pyramid went on to a world tour, a live album, two Grammys and, 20 years later, a LEGO set. The crowd count and the bands it started are legends; the rest is on the record.
- [The moments](https://polo.cold.fyi/moments/): The sets people still bring up, and what the paperwork says happened. A Prince cover that kept getting pulled offline, a dead rapper reflected off a sheet of foil, a homecoming with about 200 people on stage, an ice rink that outlasted its headliner, and a $2.5M concrete bunker for a band that never showed up.
- [What Coachella started](https://polo.cold.fyi/started/): The things that left the polo field and kept going: reunions that became world tours (one grossed $584.2M), a second weekend Austin City Limits copied, and a webcast that once made you "like" a gum brand and is now a YouTube exclusive through 2030. Then a look, a suffix, a payment plan, a family of spin-off festivals and a food truck. Coachella rarely invented these things. More often it was the biggest stage they ever got.
- [Getting there](https://polo.cold.fyi/getting-there/): About 40,000 people a day ride a shuttle into Indio, and the company that runs it isn't Goldenvoice - it's a travel outfit owned, three layers up, by the company behind UFC and WWE. The drivers come from all over, the train ran exactly once, and the rich fly into a WWII airfield in Thermal. Everyone else sits on Jefferson Street, then leaves on Monday at 9 a.m.
- [Camping and the rituals](https://polo.cold.fyi/camping/): Camping began in 2003 and cars joined in 2010; now about 35,000 people sleep on the grounds. The festival starts for them on Thursday - in a Walmart lot, a Ralphs lot, a 12-hour line, and since 2025 at Goldenvoice's own campers-only party, Day 0. Along the way: a gospel service on a hill built in a week, horses, hot dogs, an iron fence and a wristband scam.
- [The lineup and the poster](https://polo.cold.fyi/lineup/): One man reads thousands of pitches a year, picks about 150 acts, and sets every name on the poster in one typeface at one of several sizes - a size agents fight over. The poster used to land in January. Now it lands in the fall: the 2027 passes went on sale in May with no names on them, and the poster followed on Nov. 10, 2026, with a fourth headliner and no day for him. Behind it sits a radius clause that keeps those names off other stages from December to May, and a small Portland festival that sued over it.
- [The build, the art, the ticket, the food](https://polo.cold.fyi/build/): Coachella is built from an empty polo field in about five weeks, and taken down again in time for Stagecoach. That means a PA crew that has done it for nearly two decades, a tent standing on 1,500 tons of concrete, a curfew that bills by the minute, a livestream directed with no rehearsals, and an ex-Hollywood effects man who builds the biggest thing that can go up in ten days. Then there is the wristband that gets you in, most often bought on a payment plan, and a four-course dinner in a rose garden.
- [The money and Indio](https://polo.cold.fyi/money/): The last published gross is $114.6M, for 2017. Since then the festival's own numbers have gone quiet, and the figures that do get printed come from the city, the tourism bureau or the governor's office, none of them an independent audit. Indio settled for a few dollars a ticket after a 2012 standoff, and in 2024 that came to just over $2M. The people who clean the field overnight are often the same people who pick the valley's grapes.
- [The valley and the season](https://polo.cold.fyi/season/): Coachella is two weekends in a longer desert season. The same polo field hosts a country festival the week after, which outsold it in 2024, and has held classic-rock and metal festivals in October. An art biennial puts billboards on the road into Palm Springs, parties fill hangars and horse parks, and pool parties take over in August. The festival is named for a valley and held in Indio, while the city actually called Coachella is its own place, in a part of the valley the festival rarely touches.
- [The billboards on the I-10](https://polo.cold.fyi/billboards/): Every spring, artists and labels rent billboards on the interstate between Los Angeles and Indio, because there is one road in and the people driving it are exactly the people they want. The boards cost from about $8K to $40K for a few weeks, and one 2026 campaign reportedly ran to $1M. This is a sourced, year-by-year archive of them, from the first ones on record in 2013 to the 20 that were booked for 2020 and never went up.

- Data: https://polo.cold.fyi/lineup-2027.json, https://polo.cold.fyi/lineup-2027.csv, https://polo.cold.fyi/lineup-2027.txt, calendar https://polo.cold.fyi/coachella-2027.ics
- Weekends 2027-04-09 to 2027-04-11 and 2027-04-16 to 2027-04-18; the same lineup plays both. Set times and stages not published as of 2026-11-11.
- Friday (2027-04-09, 2027-04-16): headliner Dua Lipa; then Madonna (in the dance tent), Zara Larsson, Steve Lacy, JISOO, Diljit Dosanjh, Peggy Gou, Kehlani, Solid Grooves, Giorgio Moroder, Social Distortion, Pinegrove, Angine de Poitrine, Leon Thomas, Drain Gang, Snow Strippers, Mike D 5D, CHRIS STASSY, Milo J, SG Lewis, Kelela, Franky Rizardo, Fetty Wap, Vintage Culture, the Damned, ATARASHII GAKKO!, Nettspend, American Football, xaviersobased, La Dispute, Haute & Freddy, the Hellp, Disco Dom, MPH, Bella Kay, This Is Lorelei, the Womack Sisters, mary in the junkyard, Close Friends Only, Obskür, Jacob Lusk, LEENALCHI, Bea Miller, Gang of Youths, Love Spells, Rafael, Nirosta Steel, Ragie Ban, Eli, Las Petunias, Violet Grohl, Jackie Hollander, Jamback x Marsolo, NOYA
- Saturday (2027-04-10, 2027-04-17): headliner Tame Impala; then Phoebe Bridgers, Weezer, Tiësto, Martin Garrix, Robyn, Role Model, ADÉLA, Måneskin, Solomun, NCT, Enigma, Underworld, Charlotte de Witte, Leon Bridges, Cloonee, Magdalena Bay, Barry Can't Swim, Boy Harsher, KI/KI, Mariah the Scientist, Bad Gyal, Basement, Brutalismus 3000, Beltran, underscores, SB19, Twin Tribes, Odeal, Bassvictim, Los Pibes Chorros, Tiffany Day, no na, Mathame, ear, Vandelux, rommulas, Apollonia, Getdown Services, Good Neighbours, First Day Back, Jimi Jules, Twisted Teens, Murda Beatz, Villanelle, Kolter x Sidney Charles, La Texana, OMRI., Volkoder, Zimmer90, LuSiD, Dream Boat
- Sunday (2027-04-11, 2027-04-18): headliner SZA; then Don Toliver, DOM DOLLA, Kygo, Empire of the Sun, Four Tet, the Neighbourhood, Becky G, BABYMONSTER, Amelie Lens x Sara Landry, Remi Wolf, Tove Lo, Victoria Monét, EsDeeKid, Caroline Polachek, Chase & Status, MUNA, Boris Brejcha, Jorja Smith, the Avalanches, BOLO, Pennywise, Freddie Gibbs, Shygirl, Julia Wolf, Odd Mob, Ayra Starr, Lambrini Girls, AKRIILA, Dinner Party, Silva Bumpa, DJ Habibeats, Chanel Beads, Adam Ten, After, Zack Fox, Fat Dog, Omar+, Genesis Owusu, Joshua Slone, the Mainliners, Marten Lou x Alex Wann, ChaseWest, Florence Road, Jazzy, TUL8TE, Jakob Nowell and THE CASTLE, Talón, Klave Efectiva
- Daddy Yankee: billed "In the Desert", no day announced. Printed on its own line under Sunday with no day. Reported as a fourth headliner in a 'special production'; day not announced.
- Justice: billed "The Bunker Debut Of JUSTICE - BLINDED BY THE LIGHTS", no day announced. Printed at the foot of the poster with no day. In 2026 the same slot read 'The Bunker Debut of Radiohead Kid A Mnesia' and was an underground cinema on the grounds; what Justice's piece is had not been announced as of Nov. 11, 2026.
